intent: Change two things from iteration 4: wheel_track from 0.10 back to 0.12 m, and the sensor lead from y = 0.07 to y = 0.06 m. Keep the 16 mm sensors, the 0.16 m spread, the body, wheel radius and mass, and the 25-per-metre weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the Integrator needs no gain change. Expected result: s-bend steering_oscillation falls to at or below 0.15, slalom line_loss_events fall to about zero, and oval progress stays near 0.1175. Oval progress is not expected to move, because it was identical at both track widths. The s-bend progress may fall somewhat from 0.17. Please report progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation for each track separately.
learning: Hypothesis A (over-response): the narrow 0.10 track plus the 0.07 lead pushed s-bend and slalom oscillation past the limit, so the slalom line losses come from over-correction, not missed coverage. If this holds, s-bend oscillation falls below 0.15 and slalom line losses go to zero at y = 0.06. Hypothesis B (lead too short): the s-bend progress gain came from the forward lead, so progress falls noticeably at y = 0.06. If progress drops below 0.12 on the s-bend, I will restore y = 0.07 and keep the 0.12 track. Oval progress is flat at 0.1175 across all three races with max_error at the 0.06 floor, so oval progress is not limited by turn authority or the lead, and the next oval lever will need to be tested separately.
rationale: Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.10, y = 0.07) scored 56.50, the best so far, but its telemetry triggers the Integrator's second rule. Oval progress stayed at 0.1175, identical to the 0.12 track in iteration 3, and max_error stayed at the 0.06 floor, so narrowing the track did not add oval turn authority. Meanwhile the s-bend steering_oscillation rose to 0.164, above the 0.15 limit, and the slalom lost the line 0.95 times per run. The Integrator's pre-race feedback says these two conditions mean the track is over-responding, so the correct move is to return wheel_track to 0.12 and pull the lead back to y = 0.06. I am not applying the Integrator's third rule (mass 0.6), because that rule applies only at wheel_track 0.10 and the second rule takes priority. Sensor footprint (16 mm), spread (x = -0.08 to 0.08), body and wheel radius, and the 25-per-metre weights are unchanged, so this race isolates the lead and track change. Expected result: slalom line losses fall to near zero and s-bend oscillation drops below 0.15. I expect s-bend progress to fall somewhat from 0.17, toward the 0.13 to 0.16 range, and the score to stay near the iteration 3 to 4 level, around 54 to 57. If progress drops below about 0.12 on the s-bend, the lead is too short and the next test should be y = 0.07 with wheel_track 0.12, which is the iteration 3 design.
